Thermoregulation is a homeostatic mechanism that aims to maintain a constant core body temperature

![](/content/exams/anzca/2015/A/15/standard-image12.jpeg){fig-alt="Thermoregulation feedback system showing thermal sensors, hypothalamic controller and autonomic and behavioural effectors"}

Interthreshold range is the range of core temperatures over which no autonomic thermoregulatory responses occur. Approx. 37C +/- 0.2C in non-anaesthetised state

**General Anaesthesia effects on Thermoregulation:**

GA causes 1-3C core body temperature over 3 phases

Phase 1 

- Occurs over first 30min-1 hour  
- ↓1.5C initial rapid phase of loss due peripheral vasodilation and subsequent heat loss from redistribution from core to peripheries
- Inter-threshold range is increased from 0.4°C to 4°C

Phase 2

- Further core temperature drop over \~2hours of \~1°C 
- Heat loss is a result of heat loss exceeding heat production as non-shivering thermogenesis is only response available to paralysed anaesthetised patient

Phase 3 Plateau

- Thermoregulatory responses are activated and vasoconstriction constrains heat to core 
- Increased metabolic heat production
- Heat loss may still exceed heat production 

**Neuraxial Anaesthesia effects on Thermoregulation:**

- Hypothermia is generally less extreme as thermoregulation is only affected in areas covered by blockade → larger the blockade →↑effect on thermoregulation and temperature 
- Plateau phase does not occur  as vasoconstrictive responses are inhibited by the blockade
